distinguishing_features: Solid thin-film sacrificial metal-oxide coating (TiO2/WO3) applied by ALD, rather than a liquid inhibitor dosed into the electrolyte
Localized, solid-state charge-redistribution anodic pathway at the plate surface during transients, rather than bulk electrolyte E_pit shifting by molybdate complexation
Passive, no-active-control operation via a permanent surface film, rather than schedule-driven pump dosing
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Mitigate localized anodic dissolution and pit initiation at bipolar plates during start-stop current transients while maintaining surface conductivity and avoiding added active dosing infrastructure
parsed.viable_reason: A thin ALD oxide overlayer on a conductive underlayer is physically plausible at 100-200 nm, the corrosion-rate arithmetic is self-consistent, and the 100-cycle polarization test can validate the stated i_corr reduction.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Sacrificial/anodic-shift oxide layers as an anti-corrosion strategy fall squarely within the closest prior art's class of oxide-chemistry passivation (molybdate film stabilization), so applying an oxide barrier atop a conductive underlayer is a routine substitution of a solid-film form for a dosed-inhibitor form rather than a non-obvious mechanism.
